# Upgrading from 0.22.x to 0.23.x


<Warning>
  0.23 also removes project workers declared in `config.yaml`, the `iii worker` command, and the
  `worker::*` functions. Before you install 0.23, do the pre-upgrade actions in Steps 1 and 2 on
  0.22.x: stop publishers, let active work drain, and back up the queue data. Then complete [Move
  workers from config.yaml to Compose](./workers-to-compose) before you start the project on 0.23.
</Warning>

0.23.x adds namespaces. Workers that declare no namespace land in `default` and behave as before, so
most projects upgrade with no code change. Apply the steps below that touch surfaces your project
uses. Steps 4 and 5 apply only to workers that move out of `default`. Step 1 applies to those
workers and to a subscriber whose function id contains `@` or `\`.

## Step 1: Redeclare RabbitMQ durable subscriber queues

A durable subscriber in `default` keeps its queue name, so it keeps its queue and its messages. A
function id that contains `@` or a backslash is the exception. The queue worker escapes that
function id, so that subscriber gets a new queue. A subscriber in any other namespace uses a queue
name that includes the namespace. Subscribers of the same topic and function id in different
namespaces then use separate queues.

| Subscriber namespace | Subscriber queue                       | Dead-letter queue                    |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `default`            | `iii.{topic}.{function_id}.queue`      | `iii.{topic}.{function_id}.dlq`      |
| Other                | `iii.{topic}.{function_id}@{ns}.queue` | `iii.{topic}.{function_id}@{ns}.dlq` |

`{ns}` is the subscriber's namespace. The queue worker puts a backslash before each `@` and `\` in
the function id and in the namespace.

When a subscriber moves out of `default`, it declares and consumes a new queue. The queue worker
does not rename, consume, or migrate the old queue. The old queue and its binding stay in RabbitMQ
until you delete the queue. The binding continues to send copies of new events to the old queue.

<Warning>
  Before a subscriber moves out of `default`, drain its old queue. No consumer reads the old queue
  after the move.
</Warning>

For each subscriber that moves out of `default`, or whose function id contains `@` or `\`:

1. Stop publishing to the topic.
2. Let the existing consumers drain the old queue to empty.
3. Upgrade, or move the subscriber to its namespace, and restart it. The queue worker declares the
   new queue on the next subscribe.
4. Delete the drained queue and its dead-letter queue from the broker.

A Compose project that runs in a namespace other than `default`, for example with
`iii compose --namespace dev`, moves every subscriber in the project.

## Step 2: Preserve queue storage before moving the worker

The queue implementation is no longer supplied by the engine. Before upgrading, stop publishing and
let 0.22.x drain active work, then move `iii-queue` to the standalone `queue` Compose package. Keep
the same `file_path` or broker settings under its `config_override`; changing the path creates an
empty store and leaves the old jobs behind.

Follow the queue row in [Move workers from config.yaml to Compose](./workers-to-compose). Compose
does not copy the stored `iii-queue` configuration. Before you upgrade, read it with
`iii trigger configuration::get id=iii-queue raw=true` so that its `${VAR}` templates stay intact.
Put the returned `value` under the queue container's `config_override`. To find the configuration id
that the queue container reads, see
[Readable configuration names and migration](../using-iii/compose#readable-configuration-names-and-migration).
Back up the queue data before the first 0.23 start. iii does not rewrite or relocate it
automatically.

## Step 3: Tune the registration grace period, if needed

A connection that does not send `engine::workers::register` within the grace period lands in
`default`. The default grace period is 5000 ms. If workers on slow links land in `default`
unexpectedly, raise it under `engine:` in `worker-compose.yaml`:

```yaml worker-compose.yaml
engine:
  registration_namespace_grace_ms: 10000
```

To apply the change, stop `iii compose --up` and start it again. An engine that reads `config.yaml`
directly takes the same field at the top level of `config.yaml`. To set the value with
`III_NAMESPACE_GRACE_MS`, see
[Set the namespace registration timeout](../using-iii/engine#set-the-namespace-registration-timeout).

## Step 4: Check for `engine::*` function ids outside `default`

<Note>
  Most custom workers do not use the `engine::` prefix. Check this step because the new rule rejects
  an existing custom function that uses the prefix outside `default`.
</Note>

Every worker has a namespace. A worker uses `default` if you do not specify a namespace. `engine::*`
is reserved for engine infrastructure, which is registered in `default`. If a worker in a
non-default namespace registers an `engine::*` function id, the engine rejects that registration
with `FUNCTION_NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`. The connection stays open, and its other functions continue to
serve requests. Rename the function with your own `service::name` prefix.

The standalone queue worker registers five `engine::queue::*` functions in its own project
namespace: `engine::queue::enqueue`, `engine::queue::list_topics`, `engine::queue::topic_stats`,
`engine::queue::dlq_topics`, and `engine::queue::dlq_messages`. The engine allows these five ids in
every namespace. The rule rejects every other `engine::*` id that a worker registers outside
`default`.

## Step 5: Scope RBAC rules when adopting a namespace

Two RBAC surfaces changed, and both matter only for a worker that leaves `default`.

First, `expose_functions` rules on the `iii-worker-manager` RBAC listener are namespace-scoped. A
rule that names no namespace applies to `default` only, so it will not expose a function reached in
another namespace. When you move a worker into a namespace, scope its rules to match:

```yaml
expose_functions:
  - match: "orders::*"
    namespace: orders
```

Add one rule for each namespace the session reaches. See
[Namespace-scoped function rules](../creating-workers/worker-manager#namespace-scoped-function-rules)
for the matching syntax.

Second, `allowed_functions` on the auth result now applies in `default` only. It used to apply in
every namespace, so a grant issued for one tenant answered for every other tenant exposing the same
function id. If your auth function returns `allowed_functions` for a worker that runs in a
namespace, move those grants into `namespaces`, which the auth result now carries. See
[Scope a session to namespaces](../creating-workers/worker-manager#scope-a-session-to-namespaces).

`forbidden_functions` is unchanged and still applies in every namespace. An auth function that
returns no `namespaces` keeps the behavior it had.

## Migration checklist

- [ ] Drain and delete the old RabbitMQ queues of subscribers that move out of `default` or whose
      function id contains `@` or `\` (Step 1)
- [ ] Stop publishers and drain active `iii-queue` jobs before the upgrade (Step 2)
- [ ] Back up the queue data and preserve its `file_path` or broker settings (Step 2)
- [ ] Copy the stored `iii-queue` configuration into the queue container's `config_override`
      (Step 2)
- [ ] Raise `registration_namespace_grace_ms` if workers land in `default` unexpectedly (Step 3)
- [ ] Rename `engine::*` function ids registered by namespaced workers (Step 4)
- [ ] Add `namespace:` to `expose_functions` rules for namespaced workers (Step 5)
- [ ] Move `allowed_functions` grants for namespaced workers into `namespaces` (Step 5)

## Result

The project runs on 0.23.x. Workers that declare no namespace keep routing through `default` as they
did on 0.22.x, and their durable subscriptions keep their queues unless the function id contains `@`
or `\`. Workers that declare a namespace own their function ids in it, and their durable
subscriptions consume from namespace-qualified queues.

<Note>
  To configure workers and calls, see [Use namespaces](../using-iii/namespaces). To understand
  strict routing, see [Namespaces](../understanding-iii/namespaces).
</Note>
